subclassFeature.name: Warrior of the Mystic Arts
entries: Warriors of the Mystic Arts wield magic to supplement their martial skill. They harness mystical focus to enhance their magical and physical abilities.

subclassFeature.name: Spellcasting
entries: You have learned to cast spells. See the {@book Player's Handbook|XPHB} for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules as a Warrior of the Mystic Arts.

entries.name: Cantrips
entries: You know two cantrips of your choice from the {@filter Sorcerer spell list|spells|class=Sorcerer}. {@spell Blade Ward|XPHB} and {@spell Thunderclap|XPHB} are recommended. Whenever you gain a Monk level, you can replace one of these cantrips with another cantrip of your choice from the {@filter Sorcerer spell list|spells|class=Sorcerer}.
When you reach Monk level 10, you learn another {@filter Sorcerer cantrip|spells|level=0|class=Sorcerer} of your choice.

entries.name: Spell Slots
entries: The Warrior of the Mystic Arts Spellcasting table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Prepared Spells of Level 1+
entries: You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose three level 1 spells from the {@filter Sorcerer spell list|spells|class=Sorcerer}. {@spell Jump|XPHB}, {@spell Magic Missile|XPHB}, and {@spell Shield|XPHB} are recommended.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Monk levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Warrior of the Mystic Arts Spellcasting table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional spells from the {@filter Sorcerer spell list|spells|class=Sorcerer} until the number of spells on your list matches the number on the table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you're a level 7 Monk, your list of prepared spells can include five Sorcerer spells of levels 1 and 2 in any combination.

entries.name: Changing Your Prepared Spells
entries: Whenever you gain a Monk level, you can replace one spell on your list with another {@filter Sorcerer spell|spells|class=Sorcerer} for which you have spell slots.

entries.name: Spellcasting Ability
entries: Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for your Sorcerer spells.

entries.name: Spellcasting Focus
entries: You can use an {@item Arcane Focus|XPHB} as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB} for your Sorcerer spells.

entries.name: Multiclassing
entries: If you multiclass and have the Spellcasting feature from more than one class, add one third of your Monk levels (round down) to determine your available spell slots.

subclassFeature.name: Mystic Fighting Style
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn, you can replace one {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} with a casting of one of your Sorcerer cantrips that has a casting time of an action.

subclassFeature.name: Mystic Focus
entries: You keep your magical power and martial focus in perfect balance, allowing you to convert spell slots into Focus Points, or convert Focus Points into spell slots.

entries.name: Converting Spell Slots to Focus Points
entries: You can expend a spell slot to regain a number of expended Focus Points equal to the slot's level (no action required).

entries.name: Recovering Spell Slots
entries: When you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} or use Uncanny Metabolism, you can transform unexpended Focus Points to recover one expended spell slot. The Recovering Spell Slots table shows the cost of recovering a spell slot of a given level, and it lists the minimum Monk level you must be to recover a slot. You can recover a spell slot no higher than level 4.

subclassFeature.name: Focused Strike
entries: When you use your Stunning Strike, whether the target succeeds or fails on the saving throw, the target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on saving throws against your spells until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Improved Mystic Fighting Style
entries: When you use Flurry of Blows, you can replace two of the {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes} with a casting of one of your level 1 or 2 Sorcerer spells that has a casting time of an action, and you cast it as part of the same {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} you use to activate Flurry of Blows.
